context_requirements: Functional mitochondrial electron transport chain (complexes I-IV)
Ability to mount integrated stress response (ATF4/CHOP axis)
Aerobic metabolism or dependence on oxidative phosphorylation
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation or cell-cycle genes at 24 h in any line
No induction of apoptosis or stress-response genes at 24 h
No change in mitochondrial or oxidative-stress gene signatures
Uniform lack of response across all nine lines

evidence.supports: Antimycin A inhibits A549 growth via G1 arrest, apoptosis, and increased ROS
Antimycin A induces G1 arrest and apoptosis in Calu-6 lung cancer cells
Antimycin A causes cytochrome c release and caspase-3 activation

changes: Removed PMID 17690326: abstract reports rotenone/antimycin inhibit Siglec-8-mediated eosinophil apoptosis, contradicting the stated claim that they inhibit mitochondrial/ROS-dependent apoptosis as a general pro-apoptotic mechanism.

Removed generic proliferation genes (MCM3, PCNA, TOP2A, AURKA, AURKB, PLK1, BUB1B, CDC20, CCNB1, CCNB2) from proximal_down; these are generic proliferation markers, not immediate transcriptional targets of electron transport inhibition.
Removed generic stress/apoptosis genes (BAX, BID, CASP3, CASP7, CASP10, DFFA, DFFB, GADD45B) from late_up; these are generic apoptosis/stress effectors rather than specific proximal readouts.
Kept HIF1A, DDIT4, BNIP3, BNIP3L, NFE2L2, HMOX1, SQSTM1, TRIB3, CHAC1, ATF5, SESN1, GADD45A as justified stress/hypoxia/ISR targets of mitochondrial inhibition.
Kept MYC, CCND1, CCNE2, CDK4, CDK6 in down lists as consistent with G1 arrest reported for antimycin A.
Kinetics 'slow' and magnitude weak/moderate are consistent with the 6 h/24 h design and the cited 72 h growth-inhibition assays.
